# Findings

One file per measurement, newest first. `verdict` is the whole result —
open the file for the method. A finding says what is *true about the
system* and outlives the code that prompted it; a work item says what
was built.

| Date | Finding | Status | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-06 | [v2 never exercised its kernel dispatch's variability](2026.08.06-v2-kernel-shape-census.md) | closed | All ten v2 filters register CPU-only through three of dispatch.py's four protocols — zero merging, zero GPU — and all three are projections of one run(params, window, state) signature. |
| 2026-08-06 | [The synthetic fixture identifies frames by order, not by the value it wrote](2026.08.06-the-synthetic-fixture-identifies-frames-by-order.md) | closed | Round-tripped through mp4v, frame `n`'s blue field comes back at `n * 5 - δ` with δ up to 4 of the 5 levels between neighbours — uniform to the pixel and strictly increasing, but never the written value. Frame identity is carried by the ordering; a test asserting `n * 5` back out of the decoder is asserting the codec. |
| 2026-08-06 | [The scaffold's 72-column annotation does not fit 37% of the modules v3 will port](2026.08.06-the-scaffold-annotation-does-not-fit-a-ported-module.md) | closed | 46 of v2's 124 module docstrings open with a line longer than 72 characters, and 5 more open with a wrapped fragment that is not a sentence — so `doc_index.ANNOTATION_LIMIT` and the "first line is the annotation" rule both fail on verbatim ports rather than on a single unlucky file. |
| 2026-08-06 | [Every contract goes red on one line, uninstalled packages included](2026.08.06-every-contract-goes-red-on-one-line.md) | closed | All five contracts fail on a single added import each, and PySide6/cv2 are caught while absent from the venv — the forbidden externals need never be installed for `headless` and `opencv-containment` to bind. |
| 2026-08-06 | [A derived doc proves the copy, not the decision](2026.08.06-derived-docs-prove-the-copy-not-the-decision.md) | open | SCAFFOLD's derivation makes it impossible for the tree to disagree with the docstrings and does nothing about the docstrings disagreeing with the ADRs — `core`'s ownership line already omits schema v1, an ADR-6 member, and every gate in the repo passes. |
| 2026-08-06 | [A forbidden module that does not exist yet is silently inert](2026.08.06-a-forbidden-module-that-does-not-exist-is-inert.md) | open | `gui -> sieve.core.ops` passes `lint-imports` today and breaks it the moment `src/sieve/core/ops/` exists — import-linter matches forbidden modules against the graph, so an entry naming nothing is unenforced and unreported, and a typo there would never surface. |

## Loop

Truths about how the work loop fails rather than about the system —
what the review prompt is distilled from.

| Date | Finding | Status | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-07 | [The review prompt has no path for a partial deferral](loop/2026.08.07-the-review-prompt-has-no-path-for-a-partial-deferral.md) | open | The review prompt's deferral branch says amend `done_when` and set the item back to `open`, which assumes the amendment leaves work — but 01.2 committed everything except the struck part, so the amended criterion passed on the tree as reviewed and `open` would have queued a work run with nothing to do. This review set `done` instead and is saying so rather than quietly widening the branch. |
| 2026-08-07 | [An item at awaiting-review leaves the selection rule and never returns](loop/2026.08.07-awaiting-review-leaves-the-selection-rule-and-never-returns.md) | open | `--next` answers with the lowest *open* step, so the moment a worker writes `awaiting-review` the item stops being selectable, and nothing in the repo emits the review that would move it on — the queue entry naming it is typed by hand. When the entry after 00.3's work run said "continue the loop" instead of "review 00.3", the item left the loop for good: selection is monotone in step order, so a low step sitting at awaiting-review is passed and never approached again. It happened twice in a row and nothing went red. |
| 2026-08-07 | [A criterion drafted from v2's file list names a subject two phases out](loop/2026.08.07-a-criterion-drafted-from-v2s-file-list-names-a-subject-two-phases-out.md) | open | 01.2's `done_when` named `tests/unit/test_tool_discovery.py` because v2 has a `test_filter_discovery.py` beside its `test_filter_contract.py` — but all six of that file's cases need a shelf that arrives at 02.4, so the criterion was unreachable from the day it was written and nothing between writing it and the worker reaching it would have said so. |
| 2026-08-06 | [One red per contract certifies the contract, not each of its lines](loop/2026.08.06-one-red-per-contract-certifies-the-contract-not-its-lines.md) | open | A proof-of-red that adds one violating edge per contract proves the contract is wired up and leaves every other line in it untested — in 00.2 the single untested line was also the only one that could not fire, and the finding's verdict generalised over it anyway. |

*10 findings.*
